sections.headline: Tech Stocks Drive Market Higher
sections.body: Traders are watching the performance of megacap tech stocks, which rose as the S&P 500 climbed to a new high [2]. The market's resilience in the face of rising bond yields suggests that investors are shrugging off concerns about inflation [3]. This trend is also reflected in the Nasdaq's record high, which rose alongside the S&P 500 [2].

sections.headline: Nasdaq Reaches Record High
sections.body: The Nasdaq's record high was driven by a strong performance from megacap tech stocks, which rose despite high treasury yields. This suggests that investors are prioritizing growth over interest rate concerns. [5]

sections.headline: Yields Rise Amid Bull Market
sections.body: Traders are watching the Fed minutes release, which is expected to provide insight into the central bank's future interest rate decisions. A strong reading could lead to higher yields, while a weak one might calm market nerves. The rising yields are also seen as a sign of a strong economy, which is supporting the bull market in stocks.

sections.headline: US Dollar Strengthens vs Yen
sections.body: The US Dollar strengthened against the Japanese Yen due to rising US yields, which revived dollar buying, according to finance.biggo.com [11]. This move was also supported by a wide yield gap, which FXStreet [12] noted. Traders are watching the NFP data, which eased Fed concerns and led to a decrease in the Yen's value, as seen in the USD/JPY analysis by StoneX [14].

sections.headline: Oil Prices Fall Amid Middle East Concerns
sections.body: Crude oil prices fell due to concerns about shipping risks in the Middle East, despite a planned release of crude and diesel by the G-7, according to the WSJ [15]. This move was partly offset by a rise in Middle East crude exports, as reported by the EIA [1]. Traders are watching the situation closely, with some stocks holding near their records despite the oil price drop [17].

sections.headline: Gold Rises on Rate Hike Fears

The S&P 500's continued climb despite struggles with higher rates suggests that investors are still optimistic about the market, but gold's price is being driven by concerns about the economy. The gold price is also being influenced by the decline in crude prices, which is making stocks more attractive.

brief:
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq reached new highs, driven by strong performances from megacap tech stocks, as investors prioritized growth over interest rate concerns.

S&P 500 (+0.81% to 7785.49): Tech Stocks Drive Market Higher. Traders are watching the performance of megacap tech stocks, which rose as the S&P 500 climbed to a new high [2]. The market's resilience in the face of rising bond yields suggests that investors are shrugging off concerns about inflation [3]. This trend is also reflected in the Nasdaq's record high, which rose alongside the S&P 500 [2].
Nasdaq (+1.18% to 27512.48): Nasdaq Reaches Record High. The Nasdaq's record high was driven by a strong performance from megacap tech stocks, which rose despite high treasury yields. This suggests that investors are prioritizing growth over interest rate concerns. [5]
10-Year Yield (+0.64% to 5.31): Yields Rise Amid Bull Market. Traders are watching the Fed minutes release, which is expected to provide insight into the central bank's future interest rate decisions. A strong reading could lead to higher yields, while a weak one might calm market nerves. The rising yields are also seen as a sign of a strong economy, which is supporting the bull market in stocks.
USD/JPY (+0.01% to 157.94): US Dollar Strengthens vs Yen. The US Dollar strengthened against the Japanese Yen due to rising US yields, which revived dollar buying, according to finance.biggo.com [11]. This move was also supported by a wide yield gap, which FXStreet [12] noted. Traders are watching the NFP data, which eased Fed concerns and led to a decrease in the Yen's value, as seen in the USD/JPY analysis by StoneX [14].
Crude Oil (-2.33% to 88.99): Oil Prices Fall Amid Middle East Concerns. Crude oil prices fell due to concerns about shipping risks in the Middle East, despite a planned release of crude and diesel by the G-7, according to the WSJ [15]. This move was partly offset by a rise in Middle East crude exports, as reported by the EIA [1]. Traders are watching the situation closely, with some stocks holding near their records despite the oil price drop [17].
Gold (+0.18% to 4170.0): Gold Rises on Rate Hike Fears. Traders are watching the impact of higher interest rates on the gold market, as a rate hike is expected to make gold more attractive as a safe-haven asset. The S&P 500's continued climb despite struggles with higher rates suggests that investors are still optimistic about the market, but gold's price is being driven by concerns about the economy. The gold price is also being influenced by the decline in crude prices, which is making stocks more attractive.

Also worth knowing:
- The Nasdaq hit a record high led by tech, with traders eyeing oil and yields.
- The Dow slipped, while the dollar strengthened as investors looked for safety.
- The Nasdaq hit a new all-time high as AI-tied stocks rose, while oil prices slipped and treasury yields surged.
